messages:
jess: quick q — our CI started hitting 401s when hitting the API from the windows runner. i'm adding the API key as a Basic header via curl but the header looks different in the failing runs. snippet i'm using:
```
# in CI job (linux example that worked locally)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n :$API_KEY | base64)" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
It works locally but fails on runner with 401. any tips?

omar: are you sure the runner is using bash vs powershell? `echo -n` is notorious on pwsh. on powershell `echo -n` will include a newline which changes the base64. try the pwsh-safe version: `powershell -Command "[Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes(':'+$env:API_KEY))"`

kai: for posix shells i prefer `printf` which avoids extra newlines/quotes: `printf ':%s' "$API_KEY" | base64`. then: `curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(printf ':%s' "$API_KEY" | base64)" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

sarah: also double-check how the secret was created in GH Actions / Vault. sometimes copy-paste adds a trailing CRLF or invisible char. quick check: `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | hexdump -C` (or on pwsh inspect bytes) — if you see 0d 0a at the end that's your culprit.

jess: ahhh that was it. the secret in our repo had a trailing CRLF (windows clipboard). removed the newline and the header now matches the working one. thanks!

omar: FYI for future-proofing, you can avoid manual base64 shenanigans by using curl's `-u` with an empty username: `curl -u :$API_KEY https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — curl will construct `Authorization: Basic` for you (but beware of shells that treat `:password` specially).

sarah: and if anyone hits this on mac/wsl, `pbpaste`/`pbcopy` can introduce EOL weirdness too. when in doubt `printf` + hexdump.

infra-bot: infra-bot: verified a successful 200 from the windows runner after secret rotation :white_check_mark:
